name: Navin Fluorine International Ltd
about: Navin Fluorine International Ltd is primary engaged in producing refrigeration gases, inorganic fluorides, specialty organofluorines and offers contract research and manufacturing services. [1] Its portfolio includes 50+ fluorinated compounds developed over the years. [2]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 23.0% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 20.8%.
EBITDA margin expanded 640 bps over 5 years (26.2% → 32.6%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 47% to 57% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 34.2%, 170 bps above a year ago.
Over 5 years: ₹1,861 cr of profit, ₹2,226 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.20x.

context.speaker: Vishad Mafatlal
context.text: Navin Fluorine's Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are our Managing Director, Mr. Nitin Kulkarni; our Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Anish Ganatra; and Ms. Payal Dave from Cygnus Partners, our Investor Relations Advisors. Before we proceed, I would like to take this opportunity to thank MUFG Intime team for supporting us in managing our Investor Relations activities during the last 5 years. We appreciate their contribution and assistance extended to us during this period. We have appointed Cygnus Partners as our Investor Relations consultant. We look forward to working with them as we continue to strengthen our engagement with the investor community. Coming to our performance in the first half of FY27, our PAT crossed INR500 crores with an EPS of INR100. This result reflects our continued focus on strengthening our business, building capabilities for the future and advancing our strategic priorities through disciplined execution. As we navigate the evolving business environment, our priority remains to strengthen our business fundamentals and deliver sustainable growth across all verticals. At the same time, the safety, health and well-being of our employees remain paramount, and we continue to uphold high standards of safety and operational excellence across our facilities. I am also pleased to share that the Board has declared an interim dividend of INR8 per equity share with a face value of INR2 per share. In our HPP business, we continue to strengthen long-term customer relationships and commercial partnerships. In this context, I would like to highlight an important development announced recently. The tenure of our existing HFO supply contract with Solstice Advanced Materials has been extended Page 2 of 16 Navin Fluorine International Limited

context.speaker: Anish Ganatra
context.text: So again, you have to look at this that when we started to do the Phase 2 cGMP 4 plant, we were already doing the warehouse all the way up to Phase 6, and we are doing ETP all the way up to Phase 5, right? So we can actually go to cGMP 5 pretty quickly with the infra there in terms of the utility, etcetera. I mean the developments that you're referring to are actually positive on 2 molecules. If you picked it up, one of the molecules has already received approval in China, and that's on fast track on FDA approval. in the U.S. market. So that will sort of probably come in. Again, the other molecule is more about the potential expansion, label expansion of darolutamide itself. Page 8 of 16 Navin Fluorine International Limited October 30, 2026 And that again has promising concepts on value. I mean we are very quick -- so the moment we see and sense the utilization of our GMP plants coming to 70%, 80%, we will be triggering off Phase 5. There is absolutely no doubt in our mind on that. And I've said this before as well, come to USD100 million number, we'll sort of be starting to knocking that door very soon, frankly.

context.speaker: Anish Ganatra
context.text: So we've got -- like I said in my last commentary, Ankur, we've got 5 molecules, new molecules that we were working on. Some of the numbers that you see, the growth that you see, which Sanjesh was asking is actually out of those molecules as well. There are campaign orders for those molecules going all the way until the end of this year and beyond as well. So there will be growth coming from there. For Nectar, we had always clarified that FY27, we would be somewhere around 60%, 65% of the PAR and the balance PAR will come into FY28. So that's the ramp-up sort of around the specialty business. And INR350 crores as a run rate, we have said about last 3 quarters. So that's what you're seeing play out as well. And it will go up because of the reasons we talked before as well.

We are focusing on specialized applications across areas such as data centers, electronics, semiconductors and defense, leveraging our expertise in fluorination chemistry and R&D capability. We are confident this business will create additional growth opportunities for us. Let me now provide a brief update on our ongoing capex programs. During the quarter, we commissioned the debottlenecking of our MPP capacity at Dahej. Our HFC capacity expansion is progressing as planned and remains on track for commissioning shortly.

In our HPP business, we continued to deliver healthy revenue growth during the quarter, supported by higher volumes and improved realization. The pricing environment for HFC remains firm, with realization improved on a sequential basis. We are also witnessing encouraging customer interest in our upcoming capacities, providing good visibility for the business going forward. Our new AHF facility has witnessed an improvement in utilization, contributing to our growth momentum and R32 capex is progressing as planned and remains on track for commissioning shortly.

In the Specialty Chemical business, we continue to see healthy growth momentum supported by strong order visibility for the second half of FY27 and beyond Our product pipeline continues to expand across both existing and new molecules, strengthening our portfolio of differentiated chemistries and supporting our growth prospects. During the quarter, we commissioned the debottlenecking of our MPP capacity at Dahej in September 2026, further enhancing our production capabilities. Moving on to CDMO business.

So that's helping the CDMO business. But essentially, this is kind of the growth explaining from the sequential from quarter-to-quarter. Here on, if you look going forward, right? The growth will come. We recently commissioned the debottlenecking at the end of September. So you should start to see growth coming in from that in the specialty even beyond where we are today because that hasn't been factored in the numbers. You will also see growth coming in HPP from the new R32 commission plant that is being commissioned shortly.
Of course, it will ramp up towards the end of this quarter, and we'll start to see some incremental sort of growth coming in this quarter, but then full ramp-up possibly in the next quarter, yes.

So we've got -- like I said in my last commentary, Ankur, we've got 5 molecules, new molecules that we were working on. Some of the numbers that you see, the growth that you see, which Sanjesh was asking is actually out of those molecules as well. There are campaign orders for those molecules going all the way until the end of this year and beyond as well. So there will be growth coming from there. For Nectar, we had always clarified that FY27, we would be somewhere around 60%, 65% of the PAR and the balance PAR will come into FY28. So that's the ramp-up sort of around the specialty business.

business.what_it_does: Fluorination-chemistry manufacturer running four verticals: HPP (HFC refrigerants including R32, plus a new AHF facility), Specialty Chemicals (multi-purpose plant capacity at Dahej, Nectar project), CDMO (cGMP plants making molecules for pharma customers) and an emerging Advanced Materials business aimed at data centres, electronics, semiconductors and defence. H1 FY27 PAT crossed INR500 crore. The inputs give no revenue split by segment.

segments.name: HPP (HFC / R32 / AHF)
segments.comment: Volumes and realisations both up in Q2 FY27, HFC pricing firm and up sequentially. A 15,000 MT R32 expansion is due to commission in Q3 FY27 and fully ramp in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.comment: Dahej MPP debottlenecking was commissioned in September 2026. Management says it is not yet in the numbers. Nectar is to run at 60-65% of PAR in FY27, with the balance in FY28.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.comment: 5 new molecules have campaign orders running to year-end and beyond. cGMP-4 Phase 2 (INR125 crore) is due by Q4 FY27, and Phase 5 will be triggered at 70-80% utilisation. Target of USD100 million by FY27.

segments.name: Advanced Materials
segments.comment: New vertical with an INR90 crore capacity capex due by Q2 FY28. Targeted at 10-15% of the enlarged business by 2030.

bull.point: Margins are beating guidance: 34.2-34.5% for four quarters against a 30% guide, FY26 at 32.7% against 30% +/-2%, and 610 bps of expansion over 3 years. ROCE is 21%.

Capacity not yet in the numbers: MPP debottlenecking was commissioned in September 2026, ahead of its Q3 FY27 target. 15,000 MT of R32 commissions in Q3 FY27 with full ramp in Q4 FY27. The CDMO has 5 new molecules with campaign orders beyond year-end. All of this sits on top of 57.1% revenue growth.
Working capital is tighter: the cash conversion cycle fell from 193 to 60 days over 3 years, and CFO/PAT was 1.2x over 5 years, so reported profit is converting to operating cash.

bear.point: Heavy capex is weighing on free cash: 5y FCF is -INR899 crore and borrowings are INR1,248 crore, with a further INR700 crore planned for FY27. Returns are back-ended, with 3x asset turn not targeted until FY29 and cGMP-4 at INR900-1,000 crore not until FY28-FY29.

Project dates slip, and the big targets cannot be checked: Chemours moved from end-Q2 to Q3 FY27, and the inputs report no CDMO revenue to test USD100 million by FY27. Management's wording softened from 'very much on track' to 'starting to knocking that door very soon'.

Management's own guides imply margin risk: they keep both a 30% long-term guide and a 32-33% range against a 34.2% run-rate, which points to 120-420 bps of expected compression. Margins have stopped expanding (flat at 34.2% for 3 quarters), and part of the current level rests on 'firm' HFC realisations.

questions: What was H1 FY27 CDMO revenue in USD? Does 'knocking that door very soon' mean USD100 million of FY27 revenue or only an exit run-rate?

Margins have held at 34.2-34.5% for four quarters. Which part of that do you expect to lose to reach your 30% long-term and 32-33% guides: HFC realisations, product mix, or new-capacity start-up costs?
What delayed Chemours from end-Q2 to Q3 FY27, and has it now been commissioned? With 5y FCF at -INR899 crore, how much of the INR700 crore FY27 capex will internal accruals actually fund?
